why: Drops the containment check entirely, leaving the resolve to escape the root the way the original join did. A raw socket sending GET /../outside.txt was measured being answered 200 with a file from outside dist. Reachability is the part worth writing down: a normalising client CANNOT get there, because WHATWG URL resolution collapses both .. and %2e%2e before the request leaves, so fetch('/../x') arrives as /x. A test driven through fetch would therefore pass against the unhardened handler and prove nothing -- the assertions sit on the resolver directly for that reason. 4 of 9 fail, the four escape shapes.
